title: Bounded Temporal-Certificate Cost and Reference Runtime Overhead Characterization Results

harness.benchmark_temporal_tolerance: huge(real64), identical in A and B and used only to neutralize the external full/half identity as a benchmark confounder
harness.arm_B: Richards temporal-history layout active with seeded derivative history
harness.timed_region: Only the repeated fmr_serialized_reference_backend%run_trial calls inside each process; fixture construction, backend initialization, checkpoint construction, test-budget preflight and process startup are excluded.

interpretation.noise_note: One of 108 O2 paired blocks has a -0.169 microsecond trial delta; all twelve O2 case-median deltas are positive. This isolated negative block is retained as measurement noise evidence and is not clipped or deleted.
interpretation.cost_shape: Within the qualified frozen matrix and this benchmark harness, the temporal machinery adds no principal Richards trajectories and exactly one defect reference_tridag per service invocation. The measured wall-clock increment is microsecond-scale on this GitHub runner.

hard_nonclaims: These timings characterize one GitHub-hosted Ubuntu runner and do not establish a universal hardware-independent runtime bound.
The full/two-half benchmark harness is not a claim that production model-certificate execution should use three principal Richards advances.
The huge external temporal tolerance is benchmark scaffolding and not a production accuracy policy.
The per-service delta is an arithmetic normalization of a fixed three-service paired trial delta, not a separately clocked isolated service benchmark.
F-PE06 does not select or recommend H_budget.
F-PE06 does not qualify BALANCED or THROUGHPUT solver policy.
F-PE06 does not authorize any mass-conservation or physical-fidelity concession.
